Replay

Player abilities

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Select two abilities in staging. Q sends a world point and E sends a direction through reliable Action.Cast requests with an explicit slot and aim convention. The tick reducer validates the player, slot, catalog ID, and cooldown, then applies the cast to World. Client prediction runs the same reducer. Rejection restores both candidate state and feedback; a full lob/zone pool rejects the cast before starting its cooldown. The authority derives the cast origin from its simulated movement, so the request needs no claimed caster position.

All six stock resources load through Godot into the saved catalog: slime lob, igniter cone, frostwave nova, battlecry buff, salvefield zone and sparkjar lob. The native generator reads the same files, and Godot gates compare the catalogs. There are 16 ability rows (zero reserved), 64 lobs and 32 standing zones in this profile. The original games and their resources remain unchanged.

The five delivery families preserve the selected original rules:

  • Lob clamps its target to range, starts up to 14 pixels from the caster and uses the integer flight duration. At expiry it delivers status to living mobs in its radius. The shared damage column is unused by the original lob judge and remains unused here. A target less than one pixel away spends cooldown but creates no lob.
  • Cone checks range and half-angle against mobs. Nova checks a caster-centered radius. Both apply scaled direct damage first, then status to survivors. Secondary reactions can hurt the crew even though those primary deliveries target mobs.
  • Buff selects self or the nearest living friend according to the row, with self fallback. Stable seat order resolves equal-distance candidates.
  • Zone clamps its placement to range and records the cast's scaled damage. It pulses damage/status onto mobs and crew, including its caster. Its remaining lifetime decrements before the modulo pulse test; expiry removes it without a final pulse.

Cooldowns, cast identities/counters, lobs, zones, credit and status consequences are saved values. Correction can remove the complete cast, and authority archives resume flight and pulse timers. emit_fold combines shared per-tick feedback from the ordinary simulation and later actions; rejecting an action also restores any earlier event it modified.

Own lobs/cones use predicted presentation. Nova/buff flashes and zones use observed state, matching the original presentation policy. Zones are ordinary observed entities, so a late spectator receives the existing patch and its remaining time. Glob discs restore the original shapes, payload colors and pulse. Flights follow the original straight path without an arc or trail. Area discs and buff bursts provide nova/reaction fills, constant standing-zone fill, and once-only wearer bursts. Cast paths provide local/remote cone tongues and recorded spread bolts. Launch/contact feedback, audio listening, and feel remain review work.

The original's owner-streamed origins and frame timing differ from this fixed-tick, server-authoritative version. Requests execute after the tick's ordinary simulation; new lobs/zones first advance on the following tick. Enemy/status/zone processing order is explicit, and stable pool/seat order replaces the original map iteration. Accepted empty casts, hostile reactions and remaining-clock pulse phase are intentional rules, not transport retries or silent live-world query fallbacks.

abilities_run.sh uses declared stationary targets and initially wounded crew, then drives normal actions from three players. A spectator joins during the standing zone. The gate exercises all six resources, freeze/shatter/spread/surge reactions, generation-aware credit, regeneration, eleven zone pulses and expiry. It compares the complete world at a shared authoritative tick. These controlled encounters do not establish full original-game parity, profile persistence or run progression.

storm_run.sh assigns slime/frost to one player character (called a runner) and spark/ignite to another, verifying that the second receives credit for shatter damage and later shock damage. It also burns/douses both targets and explicitly observes the support runner's friendly surge. Observation receipts delay each test's next consuming action until all participants have seen its prerequisite; ordinary gameplay does not use those barriers. Recorded storm/surge results include network faults, exact world comparisons and the fixture's differences from the original acts.
